topics.flagship-ru-ua: Ukraine and Russia both say a US-brokered truce is holding in a ravaged city (unnamed in the input). The truce was announced by US First Lady Melania Trump and is meant to allow aid in and let residents leave safely. Other items: a UN-backed inquiry reportedly found Russia committed war crimes by attacking Ukraine's energy grid, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held talks with Putin, Britain and Poland signed a missile deal to counter Russian drones, and Russia reportedly jailed an IT worker for 13 years for donating to Ukraine.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Jordan struck what it called terrorist positions in Syria after a church attack in Karak that killed nine, and Syrian officials reported six to seven civilian deaths. Separately, US forces in the Middle East are reportedly ready to strike Iran within 96 hours if ordered, and Iranians are bracing for possible strikes around the Israeli and US elections. Israeli forces killed at least five people in Gaza, and the UN Security Council debated Iran sanctions and the status of its nuclear programme. Reports also say the nearly 8-month-old Iran war is weighing on US midterm politics through energy costs.
topics.T15: India is evacuating tens of thousands ahead of 'very severe' Cyclone Arnab, which is due to make landfall Wednesday, with about 400,000 people needing evacuation. Japan reportedly plans to ask households to stockpile three days of food and water, which officials describe as disaster preparedness rather than a war warning. BBC Newsnight reportedly found spikes in sales of torches, radios and power banks after a government call to stock up. The remaining items are retrospective or analytical pieces on Nepal's floods, the Kumamoto quake, Hurricane Melissa and disaster misinformation.
topics.T01: Jordan acknowledged civilian casualties and expressed 'regret' over its airstrike in Syria, which it said targeted Islamic State militants. A drone strike reportedly knocked out a major power substation in Sudan's capital for over 12 hours, and Pakistan's KP governor condemned Afghan Taliban shelling of civilian areas in South Waziristan. UN experts say Myanmar's conflict death toll has passed 100,000, and MSF reported a deadly shelling in Sittwe. Other items: India-China border face-offs, Turkey-Greece Aegean friction, and Pentagon concern about drone attacks on bases.
topics.T02: Western governments warn of famine risk in Sudan as war, drought and funding cuts leave millions acutely hungry. The Security Council marked 30 years of the children and armed conflict mandate amid record violations. The remaining items are small local aid stories in Nigeria and a general piece on war and mental health.
topics.T03: An Illinois man, Matthew Unglesbee, is accused of mailing letters containing white powder to Congress. He allegedly told the FBI the powder was salt and the letters were a joke. Separately, several congressional offices, including those of Maryland lawmakers, and election officials reportedly received suspicious mail with an unidentified white substance.
topics.T04: Twenty contacts of Kenya's first Ebola Bundibugyo case were released from quarantine after 21 days of monitoring, while vaccine 'hope' was reported in DR Congo. DRC cases reportedly exceed 10,000 in its fastest-growing outbreak on record, with nearly half of confirmed patients dead. Officials are investigating how a woman diagnosed in Nigeria's capital caught the virus without travelling to DRC, and she was flown to Switzerland. Uganda has imposed a 21-day quarantine on returnees from DRC and restricted transit. A bird flu outbreak at a Utah mink farm is reportedly raising pandemic concerns.
topics.T05: Coverage is thin and mostly commentary. One outlet reports Serbian President Vučić has been ousted by a student-led movement, and the EU faces questions over its Myanmar boycott as the US reopens talks with Myanmar's military-backed government. An opinion piece discusses Maria Corina Machado's return to Caracas.
topics.T06: Unrest continues in France, where the government pledged to replace its university admissions platform in 2028 after mass protests over school funding and living costs; commentary disputes whether they are 'riots' or student protests. Violent anti-government protests are reportedly escalating in Albania, with demonstrators demanding the prime minister's resignation. Left-wing protesters reportedly clashed with police and torched vehicles in Spain after a commentator's university talk was cancelled. One outlet reports deadly riots in a Sri Lankan prison left 30 dead.
topics.T07: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi urged Iran to grant inspectors immediate access to its nuclear facilities and materials, noting the agency has lacked access to key sites since the June 2025 strikes. Iran and Russia are reportedly expanding nuclear power cooperation. Commentary also criticizes French nuclear policy and the revival of tactical nuclear weapons.
topics.T08: A terrorist attack in Belgrade shortly after midnight targeted a Gendarmerie member guarding the Israeli Embassy, and a red alert is in effect (eight outlets). Uzbekistan condemned the deadly attack on a church in Karak, Jordan. Other items: three killed in violence in Kebbi, Nigeria, an Arakan Army relocation plan for border villages, and the UAE honouring a flydubai crew for foiling a mid-air terrorist attack.
topics.T10: Items are scattered and not tied to one development. Germany must choose between joining an existing fighter programme and starting a new one, and Britain is raising defence spending. Top NATO powers pledged to commit more to defence while reaffirming the US alliance. The US DIA released its clearest image yet of China's reusable spaceplane, and the Army is reportedly examining mass battlefield burials at a scale not seen since the Korean War.
topics.T11: Israel is holding its largest military drill in years, mobilizing multiple divisions to counter border infiltrations. The US and Japan conducted a coordinated anti-ship strike during Keen Sword 27. South African President Ramaphosa is reviewing a confidential report on Iran's role in a naval exercise. Other drills include India-Singapore SIMBEX-2026, Oman's Sea Lion 2026 and India-Indonesia Garuda Shakti.
topics.T12: A University of Copenhagen breach affected over 525,000 people, including stolen PIN codes. A ransomware incident at UNM Health forced surgery cancellations and ambulance diversions, claimed by the BYOD group. A cyberattack hit email accounts at Italy's Chamber of Deputies, ENGIE confirmed a customer data breach, and researchers detailed AI-driven attacks on Japanese targets. Arctic Wolf documented over 400 incidents of spam-flooding followed by Teams impersonation of IT support.
topics.T13: The European Commission proposed giving Frontex major new powers and resources for returning irregular migrants, following the Ceuta tragedy. The UN says 36,000 people have fled violence in Ethiopia into Kenya. A large march in Madrid over the Ceuta situation was reported, and the other items are partisan commentary on migration in Ireland and the UK.
topics.T14: A shouting match erupted at the UN when Cuba's foreign minister approached the podium as US Ambassador Mike Waltz was speaking. France's deputy chief of mission in Tehran was reportedly intimidated by people claiming to be Iranian security forces, the second such incident involving French diplomats in under four months. The Belgrade attack on the Israeli Embassy guard is covered under VEO / Regional Insecurity.
topics.T16: Israeli exit polls show Netanyahu with fewer votes than his main challenger, but neither side is likely to assemble a coalition easily. In Brazil, Flavio Bolsonaro lost the presidential election to Lula, refused a Supreme Court order to surrender his passport, and reportedly left for the US; his passports were cancelled. Trump said he will respect US midterm results if elections are honest, and one outlet reports Serbian President Vučić's ouster.

bluf: Ebola remains the top-scored development: Kenya released 20 contacts of its first Bundibugyo case after 21 days of monitoring, while DR Congo reportedly has more than 10,000 cases and vaccine hope is being reported. Israeli exit polls show Netanyahu with fewer votes than his main challenger, and both sides will likely struggle to form a coalition. Jordan acknowledged civilian casualties and expressed regret over its Syria airstrike, which it said targeted Islamic State militants and followed a church attack in Karak that killed nine. Ukraine and Russia both say a US-brokered truce, announced by Melania Trump, is holding in a ravaged city to allow aid and safe departures. An Illinois man, Matthew Unglesbee, is accused of mailing white-powder letters to Congress, allegedly telling the FBI it was salt and a joke, and other congressional offices also reportedly received suspicious mail. Separately, a terrorist attack in Belgrade targeted a Gendarmerie member guarding the Israeli Embassy, and a red alert is in effect. US forces in the Middle East are also reportedly ready to strike Iran within 96 hours if ordered, while Iranians brace for possible strikes around the Israeli and US elections.
